evidence: Facility self sign-up (D14) and, in the same migration, full access after support's review with facility staff invitations (P4b), both shipped closed, with the fixes of the sign-up's adversarial review, the two read-only commands of the website's second contract, the fixes of its second review and the applicant's withdrawal (R18). 0086 ports main 0061-0063 (db49a0d, 46a173f, 08c906f) with this branch's adaptations, support's review and the review fixes (R1-R12), the website contract's R13 and R14, the second review's R15-R17, R18 and P4b's section 5, listed in 0086's header and docs/MAIN_TO_NOVU_PORT.md, and runtime-grants.sql carries its grants for a later role bootstrap. What changes: identity.organization_applications gains approval_mode (NOT NULL DEFAULT 'admin_review', metadata-only) and nullable columns for support's review (self_service_reviewed_at, self_service_reviewed_by_account_id referencing auth.accounts, self_service_review_note), support's release (self_service_released_at, self_service_released_by_account_id referencing auth.accounts, self_service_release_reason), the submitting network's keyed digest (submitter_network_digest), whether it was opened without a hold (self_service_without_hold, NOT NULL DEFAULT false, metadata-only) and when support's 7-day refusal ends (self_service_refusal_ends_at, nullable), each review and release triple set together and only on an activated self-service row, the hold and refusal only on self-service rows and the refusal only on a closed one; six partial indexes; its 0046 reviewer check is replaced by main 0062's organization_applications_review_check_self_service; identity.organization_profile_completion_challenges gains activation_attempts (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, 0-5), requested_administrator_name and requested_organization_type; new definer commands submit_self_service_organization_application(text,text,text,text,text,char), public_get_organization_application, public_record_organization_cac_result, begin_self_service_provider_enrollment, prepare_self_service_provider_activation, the read-only current_self_service_provider_enrollment(char) (R13: what the password step shows before the account exists, for a live session of a ready self-service application; it needs the control and locks, charges and ends nothing) and self_service_provider_code_state(text,text,text) (R14: whether start's code went out, the code still in force and the wait before a new one; it locks and changes nothing), activate_self_service_provider_enrollment (wrapper of the owner-only definer activate_self_service_organization_application), platform.consume_self_service_cac_quota(uuid,char,integer), and support's admin_list_self_service_facilities(text), admin_review_self_service_facility(uuid,bigint,text,text,text,text,text), admin_release_self_service_facility(uuid,bigint,text,boolean), admin_list_open_self_service_applications(text), admin_reject_self_service_application(uuid,bigint,text,boolean) and admin_waive_self_service_refusals(text,text,text) (R15: a rejection or release refuses the closed application's email and network for 7 days unless support lets the applicant retry, and the waiver lifts it; a lapse refuses no one, and a new application whose email or network had one for the CAC and product closed in the last 7 days is opened without a hold; R16: the open list ranks the applications that hold a CAC now first, counts them all and searches one CAC number); two owner-only SECURITY INVOKER helpers, granted to no role and called only from the definer commands: the lapse helper identity.lapse_stale_self_service_organization_application(text,text,text) and identity.issue_organization_profile_completion_code(text,text,text,uuid,char,text) (0056's code sending, for the approval mode its caller names, R17); two new counter tables with forced RLS and no runtime privilege; five replaced functions keep their signatures, owners and grants: identity.submit_organization_application (0052's body plus the 24-hour lapse of an abandoned self-service application), identity.begin_organization_profile_completion (0056's, which now sends a code only for a governed admin_review application and answers NULL for a self-service one, as for none, R17), platform.prune_verification_quotas (0049's body plus the two new tables), platform.consume_qoreid_quota (0049's body plus a 42501 refusal of an existing_cac lookup for a self-signed-up organization support has not reviewed, CRITIC C13) and platform.control_enabled (0040's body plus the keys provider_self_service_enabled and staff_invitations_enabled); platform.control_settings's key CHECK is replaced with the six live keys plus the two new ones, and both new controls are seeded OFF. The table has no INSERT policy, so the seed reads its FORCE row-level security setting and, only if it is on, lifts it for that one insert and restores it, as main 0098 does; a table without FORCE is left without it (R8). P4b (0086 section 5; P4's activation, list, review and release are changed in place, since 0086 is unreleased): identity.organization_applications also gains the review's self_service_granted_role and self_service_verification_method (now in the five-column review check), the administrator's own licence (self_service_admin_licence_body, self_service_admin_licence_number, self_service_admin_licence_recorded_at: set together, a known body and number pattern, only on an activated self-service row) and the early end of the first 30 days (self_service_probation_ended_at, self_service_probation_ended_by_account_id referencing auth.accounts, self_service_probation_end_reason: only on a reviewed row), all nullable, and one partial index; auth.roles gains org_admin_awaiting_review with six permissions org_admin already holds (workforce.manage, audit.read and the four outreach registration and campaign permissions), and auth.permissions gains platform.facility.unlock, granted to platform_admin, platform_super_admin and facility_review_admin (all inserted without ON CONFLICT, so an existing row stops the release, PF1); new tables identity.staff_attestation_texts (two seeded texts), identity.staff_invitations, identity.staff_invitation_sends and identity.staff_licence_attestations, with uuid keys, forced row-level security with four permissive policies, no runtime privilege and guard or no-mutation triggers; two triggers on existing tables: account_roles_review_gate (before insert or update of role_code, scope_type, facility_id, membership_id or revoked_at on auth.account_roles; at a self-signed-up organization not yet reviewed it admits only the restricted role (P0001 FACILITY_REVIEW_PENDING), at a released one no facility role (FACILITY_RELEASED), and the restricted role nowhere else (FACILITY_REVIEW_ROLE_INVALID); an organization without a self-service application is not affected) and consent_grants_self_service_probation (before insert on identity.consent_grants when break_glass: at most 5 break-glass grants per facility in 24 hours during the first 30 days after review, P0001 EMERGENCY_PROBATION_LIMIT); new SECURITY DEFINER commands granted to the Identity runtime and the schema test runtime: withdraw_self_service_provider_enrollment(char) (R18: the applicant closes its own open application from its completion session, ends its codes and sessions, audits identity.organization.self-service.withdraw and sets no refusal), record_self_service_administrator_licence(text,text), list_facility_staff(), list_facility_staff_invitations(), facility_staff_management_state(), create_staff_invitation(uuid,uuid,text,text,text,text,text,text,text,char,char,char,text), record_staff_invitation_delivery(uuid,text), resend_staff_invitation(uuid,bigint,uuid,char,char,text), revoke_staff_invitation(uuid,bigint), end_facility_staff_membership(uuid,bigint,text), change_facility_staff_role(uuid,bigint,text,text,text,text,text), open_staff_invitation(uuid,char,text,char,char), prepare_staff_invitation_acceptance(char), accept_staff_invitation_with_password(char,text), preview_staff_invitation_for_account(uuid,char,char) and accept_staff_invitation_for_account(uuid,char,char); new SECURITY DEFINER commands granted to the Identity runtime only: organization_self_service_state(uuid) (the staff context's review state), admin_list_facility_staff(uuid), admin_find_staff_invitations(text), admin_set_self_service_administrator_role(uuid,bigint,text,text,text,text,text) and admin_end_self_service_probation(uuid,bigint,text); the functions of the two triggers on existing tables are SECURITY DEFINER and granted to no role, and every other section-5 function (vocabulary, state, locks, matching and acceptance helpers, and the new tables' guard triggers) is an owner-only SECURITY INVOKER helper granted to no role. Activation now grants the restricted role org_admin_awaiting_review after recording the approval; support's list returns twelve more columns; the review takes seven arguments, needs platform.facility.unlock, records the administrator's role (none, or the clinical role the organization type and product allow, with a licence of the matching body), the verification method and the licence, replaces the restricted role with org_admin (and the clinical role, attested), and revokes the administrator's sessions; the release also revokes the organization's pending invitations, ends its memberships before revoking their roles, revokes their active consent grants (one system audit row each), expires pending access requests and revokes the sessions of accounts left without an active membership. Every P4b writer and both triggers lock the organization's self-service application row first. Nothing is dropped except the two replaced CHECK constraints; no applied migration is rewritten; no existing grant is removed. Preconditions refuse to run (in the release's dry run, so nothing changes) unless exactly one reviewer check and one control-key check exist, both control lists name exactly the six live keys, the prune deletes exactly the 0049 tables, platform.consume_qoreid_quota's body is 0049's and identity.begin_organization_profile_completion's body is 0056's (md5 of each source; the latter shown to stop the migration on a copy with another body). Proof that no existing closed application can fail the new review check: the 0046 check admits a closed row only with a reviewer and a review time and either a review reason of 8+ characters or a NULL reason (a NULL check result passes); the new check requires reviewed_at and a coalesced reason of 8+ characters and, for admin_review rows (all existing rows), a reviewer; so exactly the closed rows with a NULL review_reason pass the old check and fail the new one. Every command that closes an application writes a reason of 8+ characters, so only a direct write could leave one, and 0086 counts closed rows without a reason of 8+ characters, reviewer or review time first and raises a clear exception if any exist (shown on a copy holding one such row). Read-only preflights before signing (docs/MAIN_TO_NOVU_PORT.md lists them too): P1 select count(*) from identity.organization_applications where status in ('approved','rejected') and (review_reason is null or length(btrim(review_reason)) < 8 or reviewed_at is null or reviewed_by_account_id is null) must be 0; P2 select conrelid::regclass, conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid in ('identity.organization_applications'::regclass,'platform.control_settings'::regclass) and contype='c' must show exactly one reviewer check and one control_key check of the six keys; C2 the owner of platform.control_settings and of platform.control_enabled(text) must be the migration login (for FORCE and CREATE OR REPLACE), or the dry run stops the release with nothing changed; R8 select c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity, pg_get_userbyid(c.relowner), r.rolsuper, r.rolbypassrls from pg_class c join pg_roles r on r.oid = c.relowner where c.oid = 'platform.control_settings'::regclass: if row-level security and FORCE are both on and the owner has neither rolsuper nor rolbypassrls, stop and find out why first, since production's accountless control reads could not then work as they do; every other state is kept as it is. R17 select proc.oid::regprocedure, md5(proc.prosrc) from pg_proc proc where proc.oid in ('platform.consume_qoreid_quota(text,uuid,uuid,char,char)'::regprocedure, 'identity.begin_organization_profile_completion(text,text,text,uuid,char)'::regprocedure) must show 0049's dca2fbb737f2c747148eacc7d6e66c5f and 0056's 6c94f9fca935f41a1bbcc313d9447d04, which 0086 requires, or its dry run stops the release with nothing changed. P4b's preflights: PF1 select count(*) from auth.roles where code = 'org_admin_awaiting_review' and select count(*) from auth.permissions where code = 'platform.facility.unlock' must both be 0; PF2 select tgname from pg_trigger where tgrelid in ('auth.account_roles'::regclass, 'identity.consent_grants'::regclass) and not tgisinternal must show neither account_roles_review_gate nor consent_grants_self_service_probation; PF3 select a.email, r.role_code from auth.account_roles r join auth.accounts a on a.id = r.account_id where r.scope_type = 'platform' and r.revoked_at is null: each support reviewer must hold platform_admin, platform_super_admin, or identity_review_admin + facility_review_admin (remedy: grant the last two, never platform_admin for this purpose); PF4 capture one governed staff member's GET /api/v1/auth/session facility block, to compare after the release; PF5 select c.oid::regclass, pg_get_userbyid(c.relowner) from pg_class c where c.oid in ('auth.account_roles'::regclass, 'auth.roles'::regclass, 'auth.role_permissions'::regclass, 'auth.permissions'::regclass, 'auth.accounts'::regclass, 'identity.staff'::regclass, 'identity.staff_facility_memberships'::regclass, 'identity.facilities'::regclass, 'identity.organizations'::regclass, 'identity.organization_applications'::regclass, 'identity.consent_grants'::regclass): each owned by the migration login, or the login holds TRIGGER and REFERENCES on it; PF6 select account_id, facility_id, count(*) from identity.staff_facility_memberships where active group by 1, 2 having count(*) > 1, for the record (nothing in P4b depends on it). Backward compatibility and rollback: the previous Identity (57a94db) calls none of the new commands; its governed intake still inserts admin_review rows by default; its governed approve and reject always name a reviewer and a reason of 8+ characters, which the new check admits; the replaced governed submit, prune, consume_qoreid_quota and control_enabled keep their signatures and answers for every input the previous code sends, except three that exist only once the control has been opened: the governed submit lapses a self-service row a newer Identity left unactivated for 24 hours, an organization that signed itself up gets 42501 for an organization CAC lookup until support has reviewed it (before review its administrator holds only the restricted role, without organization.manage, so the binding match and the existing_cac charge both refuse; the previous Identity answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED), and the governed completion start sends no code for a self-service application (its answer stays the uniform accepted one); the admin console's control list returns eight rows, and the previous Identity's DTO cannot change the two new keys, which stay off (both are switched off before a rollback). P4b changes nothing else the previous Identity calls: it writes facility roles only for governed organizations, which the review gate admits; its staff context resolves restricted, reviewed and invited members from their role rows as before; the probation trigger refuses a sixth break-glass in 24 hours at a probation facility with P0001, which it answers as 429 EMERGENCY_RATE_LIMITED; it has no invitation routes. test/database/provider-self-service-rollback.integration.sql runs the previous Identity's own SQL text (governed intake, admin list, get, CAC record with the application_cac quota, approve and reject, the applicant's completion start, verify, current and complete, that start sending nothing for a self-service application with the control on and off, the existing-organization CAC binding match and its existing_cac quota for a facility that signed itself up (refused before support's review, working after it, and R7's refusal on a reviewed organization whose review columns are cleared), its staff-context query (a governed administrator unchanged; the self-signed-up administrator with the restricted role's six permissions before review and org_admin's after), the control list (eight keys) and change, the guard's control reads, the prune) as hid_identity_api_runtime on the new schema. Gate: with the control off, submit, the activation pre-check and activation raise 55000 PLATFORM_CONTROL_DISABLED:provider_self_service_enabled and write nothing; the pre-check reads the control after locking the session; the control is read from Identity's accountless context exactly as the security guard's portal check already reads it in production; under an owner that cannot bypass row-level security, with FORCE on, the gate stays closed (55000 PLATFORM_CONTROL_UNAVAILABLE). With staff_invitations_enabled off, creating, resending, changing a role, opening, preparing and accepting an invitation and the signed-in preview and accept raise 55000 PLATFORM_CONTROL_DISABLED:staff_invitations_enabled; revoking, ending a membership, the lists and the delivery record stay available; the withdrawal reads provider_self_service_enabled after locking its session. Locks until commit, measured with pg_locks on PostgreSQL 16 on a copy of the 0085 production-order database: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.organization_applications and identity.organization_profile_completion_challenges, and SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE (writes wait, reads do not) on auth.accounts (the reviewer, release and probation foreign keys), from the first statements; P4b adds SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.account_roles and identity.consent_grants (the two triggers) and on auth.roles, identity.facilities, identity.staff and identity.staff_facility_memberships (the new tables' foreign keys), and no ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on an existing table; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on platform.control_settings only in the control section, still the last statements of the file (3.1 to 5.4 ms of 138 to 169 ms in eight runs on an empty database; P4's 0086 alone took 53 to 80 ms, 4.4 to 10.8 ms of it in the control section, in four runs; the read-only commands lock nothing); replacing platform.consume_qoreid_quota and identity.begin_organization_profile_completion takes no table lock. Tests: built in production order (0001-0072, role bootstrap with the 0072-era runtime-grants.sql, then 0073-0086 with apply-migrations.mjs), the same followed by a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql, and in new-installation order (0001-0086, then role bootstrap): all 50 suites pass in each (16 in services/ehr-api/database/tests, unchanged, and 34 in services/ehr-api/test/database, 17 of them new with 0086: P4's 10 and P4b's 7, self-service-review-unlock, staff-invitations, staff-invitation-acceptance, facility-staff-management, staff-invitation-concurrency, p4b-privileges and provider-self-service-withdrawal); the 17 fail on a database built to 0085 in either order, where the other 33 pass; on P4's 0086 alone (a2c21c7) P4b's 7 new suites and the 6 P4 suites P4b changed fail and the other 43 pass; for P4, the suites catch each of 23 deliberate defects in the reviewed 0086's ported part, each of 22 in R13 and R14 and their grants, each of 34 in the second review's R15-R17 and their grants, and 25 of 27 in its review fixes, the other two being caught by the runtime verifier (the pre-check reading the control before the session's lock) and by the upgrade rehearsal (a seed that turns FORCE on); for P4b, of 37 deliberate defects in its SQL the suites catch 34, the two-connection race harness one (the application row's lock dropped from the staff commands and the review gate), and two are equivalent (redundant guards). The race harness (two connections on a committed copy) shows an accept or prepare waiting behind a release answer invalid, a role change and a release in either order leave no role on an ended membership, and a review and an account disable in either order grant nothing to a disabled account, each having waited on a lock, with no deadlock. Under a non-superuser NOBYPASSRLS definer owner (the rehearsal's owner swap) every new suite passes; of the 48 suites run there only ocr-outbox-insert fails, as it does on 0085. The plan and dry run on a 0085 database list and roll back only 0086; a dry run of 0084-0086 in one transaction on a 0083 database succeeds. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs rehearses production's order as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (baseline, role bootstrap with the baseline runtime-grants.sql, dry run, migrations, then requires that a bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql changes no runtime privilege), now also requires that the release change no existing table's row-level security or FORCE setting, and releases a baseline with FORCE lifted on platform.control_settings, where FORCE must stay off and the Identity runtime must still read platform.control_enabled from an accountless connection; it passes, and fails with a seed that always turns FORCE on; with P4b it passes again, the runtime privileges that a bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql must leave unchanged rising from P4's 2111 to 2169 (21 new commands for hid_identity_runtime, counted again for hid_identity_api_runtime, which inherits it, and 16 for hid_schema_test_runtime) and no existing table's row-level security or FORCE setting changing (156 tables). At P4's commit (a2c21c7) scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs passes; this release adds one check to it, provider_enrollment_runtime (services/identity-api/scripts/verify-provider-enrollment-runtime.mjs, the Identity runtime role end to end, including the database's own gate driven through Identity), which passes, now also proving R13's confirmation read, R14's answer when no code is sent, and the second review's fixes: the registered email closing its application and another email accepted at once from the same network, the governed completion route sending no code for a self-service application, a squatter's renewal from its own network accepted without a hold and lapsed at once by the real company, the open list's ranking, total and search, support's waiver and a retry rejection. At the integrated P4b commit both pass again: the upgrade rehearsal unchanged, and the TUF rehearsal once its historical-table check of auth.roles was made exact (every role row that existed before the upgrade unchanged, and exactly the declared org_admin_awaiting_review added, active; before that change it refused 0086's new role), with provider_enrollment_runtime running the verifier's P4b section (the restricted administrator, the review gate, the review and its sign-out, staff invitations by link and code, removal, release, the audit scan) on the upgraded database. reviewed_by is left empty for the owner.
